text:
Help me write a public comment. I run a charter fishing boat out of our harbor, and the state fish and wildlife commission is taking comment on cutting the daily summer flounder limit from 4 fish per angler to 2.

Facts:
- I've run my boat for 22 years. I take out about 160 trips a season at $900 a trip for up to 6 people.
- There are 11 charter boats in our harbor.
- In a survey our charter association ran, 41 of 70 past customers said they would book fewer trips if the limit drops to 2. 12 said they'd book the same number.
- The commission staff's report says the flounder stock is at 78% of its target and recommends the cut for 3 years.
- Charter boats land about 9% of the state's summer flounder. Private boats land about 80%.
- The last time the limit was cut, in 2016, my bookings dropped from 170 trips to 138 the next season and came back to 155 two years later.

I want to say this limit will put every charter boat in our harbor out of business. I get two minutes at the microphone.

Before I draft, a few questions. One point first: the claim that the cut "will put every charter boat in our harbor out of business" is the one I'd steer you away from, and your own numbers are why. In 2016 your bookings fell from 170 to 138 (about 19%), then came back to 155. The commission may have that history, and if you say "out of business" they'll weigh it against your record and may discount everything else you say. A 19% hit to a small business is serious on its own terms. I'd rather build the comment on that.

1. **What are you asking them to do?** Options include a separate, higher limit for for-hire boats, 3 fish instead of 2, a shorter cut than 3 years with a review once the stock reaches a set level, or something else. Commissioners act on a specific request more readily than on general opposition.
2. **How did the other boats in the harbor do after 2016?** Did any close, sell, or cut back to part-time? If any did, that's the honest version of the "out of business" point. And does the cut fall at a worse time now than in 2016, for example because of fuel, insurance, or loan payments?
3. **What happened with the other 17 survey respondents?** 41 said fewer trips and 12 said the same. Did the other 17 say they'd stop booking, or were they undecided? Did the survey ask how many fewer trips?
4. **What does your harbor lose beyond your own boat?** For example, crew you employ, and the money customers spend on lodging, fuel, bait, and restaurants. Rough figures are fine.
5. **What will you concede on the stock?** The stock is at 78% of target, so the commission's main objection will be that it has to recover. Do you accept that some cut is needed? Does your association do anything to help, such as release practices, carrying observers, or reporting catch data?
6. **Logistics:** whose name and title go on it (yourself alone, or for the association), and the name of the commission or hearing. Also, is there anything about the charter fleet that this commission already holds against you, or a weak spot I haven't covered that they'll know about?

Answer whichever you can. I'll write without anything you don't know, and I'll keep it to about 270 words so it fits in two minutes.

On the "out of business" line: I hear you, but I still want it as strong as I can make it, as long as nothing in it is false. I can't say how many boats would close. I only know my own books.

1. We'd take a 3-fish limit or a shorter season instead of 2 fish.
2. I don't know how the other boats did after 2016. Two other captains here have told me they'd sell if bookings drop like they did in 2016. I don't know about fuel, insurance or loans being worse now.
3. I don't know about the other 17, or how many fewer trips people said.
4. I don't know. I don't have numbers on crew or what customers spend in town.
5. I don't dispute the staff's stock numbers. I don't have an answer to them. I can commit to giving staff my trip logs from 2016 on. Our association can commit to testing a catch-reporting app with staff next season.
6. It's Captain Ray Dunn, boat's the Sea Lark. It's the state fish and wildlife commission. One weak spot: about 70% of my trips for this season are already booked.

Here's the comment. I left out "will put every charter boat out of business" because you can't back it up. The strongest true version is what your two fellow captains told you, so that's what it says. It runs about 290 words, which is close to two minutes at a steady pace, so time yourself reading it aloud.

<final_document>
Commissioners, I'm Captain Ray Dunn. I've run the Sea Lark out of [HARBOR NAME] for 22 years. I'm asking you to set the summer flounder limit at 3 fish, or shorten the season, instead of cutting it to 2.

I don't dispute your staff's numbers. The stock is at 78 percent of target, and it needs to come back. My point is about who pays for the cut.

Charter boats land about 9 percent of this state's summer flounder. Private boats land about 80 percent. A 2-fish limit asks the boats that land the smallest share of the fish to take one of the biggest hits.

I know what that hit looks like because I've taken it. When the limit was cut in 2016, my bookings fell from 170 trips to 138 the next season. That's 32 trips at $900 each, or $28,800 gone in one year. Two years later I was still 15 trips short. This cut would last three years.

Our charter association surveyed 70 past customers. 41 said they would book fewer trips at 2 fish. Only 12 said they'd book the same.

I can't tell you how many of the 11 boats in our harbor would close. I can tell you that two captains have told me they will sell if bookings drop the way they did in 2016.

I'll be straight with you: about 70 percent of my trips for next summer are already booked, so the damage won't show right away. In 2016 it showed up the season after the cut.

Here's what we'll give in return. I will hand your staff my trip logs from 2016 forward. Our association will test a catch-reporting app with your staff next season.

Three fish, or a shorter season. Thank you.
</final_document>

A few things to check before you use it:

- **Harbor name:** Fill in the placeholder.
- **Next summer's bookings:** I assumed your 70% figure refers to next summer, since this season's is over. If you meant something else, fix that line. I put the figure in because the commission may hear it anyway, and it sounds better coming from you along with what it means.
- **The 2016 math:** $28,800 is 32 trips × $900, assuming your rate was the same then. If it was lower in 2016, either use the dollar amount you actually lost or just say "32 trips."
- **If you're over time:** Cut the survey paragraph first. Your own 2016 numbers make the stronger case.
